Braised Red Cabbage

Served at: St. Martin's Day (Martinstag)

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 1 hour

Braised red cabbage is a traditional side dish served on St. Martin's Day (Martinstag) in Germany and parts of Europe. This sweet and tangy cabbage complements roasted meats typically enjoyed during the festival, symbolizing the harvest and the generosity of St. Martin.

Ingredients

  • 1 medium head red cabbage, shredded (about 1.5 lbs / 700 g)
  • 1 large onion, thinly sliced
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 1 apple, peeled, cored, and grated
  • 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar (60 ml)
  • 1/4 cup brown sugar (50 g)
  • 1/2 cup water (120 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
  • 2 whole cloves
  • 1 bay leaf

Method

  1. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter over medium heat.
  2. Add the sliced onion and sauté until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
  3. Add the shredded red cabbage and grated apple to the pot and stir to combine.
  4. Pour in the apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, and water. Stir well.
  5. Add the salt, pepper, cloves, and bay leaf to the pot.
  6. Cover and simmer on low heat for about 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is tender and flavors meld.
  7. Remove the cloves and bay leaf before serving.
  8. Adjust seasoning with additional salt or sugar if needed, then serve warm alongside roasted meats.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, add a splash of red wine or a tablespoon of bacon fat when sautéing the onions.
  • Use a tart apple like Granny Smith for a nice balance of sweetness and acidity.
  • This dish tastes even better when made a day ahead, allowing flavors to develop.
